_comment: Model-policy artifact for contract-toaster — us-east-1.
This file is the machine-readable record of the pinned Bedrock model matrix and
the on-demand quotas granted for each model in this account/region pair.
It is referenced by ARCHITECTURE.md (Model-selection policy) and consumed by the
eval harness to derive max_eval_parallelism and enforce rate-limiting.
Update procedure:
1. Verify quotas in AWS Console → Service Quotas → Amazon Bedrock.
2. Update granted_tpm, granted_rpm, and recertification.recertified_at below.
3. Re-derive review_throughput_ceiling and max_eval_parallelism (formulas inline).
4. Record the gold_set_run_id from the certifying eval run in recertification.
5. Open a PR; this file is governed by CODEOWNERS (admin / GC approval required).
Quarterly recertification: re-run the eval harness gold set, confirm quota figures
are still accurate, update recertification.recertified_at and gold_set_run_id.
See RUNBOOK.md → Model recertification.
CAPABILITY DESCRIPTOR (issue #562): `structured_outputs` / `prompt_caching`
on models.primary / models.critic below are read by
backend/src/model_client.py::bedrock_model_capabilities. Both are `true`
for the pinned Anthropic-native models (Claude Opus 4.8 / Sonnet 4.6 on
Bedrock support structured outputs and prompt caching); models.embedding
(Titan, not a chat model) deliberately declares neither, so it fails
closed to false for both -- absence, not a guess, is the correct answer
for a model outside the Claude chat matrix.
ROLE ORDER (issue #136, ADR 0001): the critic has the last word, so the stronger
model (Opus 4.8) is the critic. [WAS, issue #136 until #148: the cheaper Sonnet
4.6 was the reviewer.]
SAME MODEL ON BOTH PASSES (issue #148, ADR 0001 item 3): models.primary now pins
the critic's model (Opus 4.8). The two passes are built byte-identical up to a
role suffix (one tool schema, one system prompt, one cached document block), so
the critic reads the prompt cache the reviewer just wrote and each review reads
the playbook cache the previous one wrote -- and a cache entry belongs to one
model. The IAM grant for this exact foundation-model ARN already exists (it is
the critic's); the reviewer's former Sonnet 4.6 grant is removed, not kept for
rollback -- infra/lib/nested/pipeline-stack.ts PRIMARY_MODEL_ID / CRITIC_MODEL_ID
mirror models.primary / models.critic here (tests/test_pipeline_stack.py Check G
cross-checks them), so a rollback re-pins both together. What changes is the
quota: BOTH passes now draw on Opus 4.8's
40K TPM / 50 RPM, so review_throughput_ceiling and max_eval_parallelism below
are re-derived for one shared bucket. Re-measure the quota at the next
recertification; the gold set has not been re-run on this pairing.

_derivation: Bottleneck: Opus 4.8 (40,000 TPM, 50 RPM), shared by BOTH passes since issue #148
put the reviewer on the critic's model. [WAS, issue #136 until #148: the Opus
critic alone, 32 reviews/hour uncached, 53 cached, with a Sonnet 4.6 reviewer on
its own 100K-TPM quota. WAS, pre-#136: the Opus primary, 35 uncached, 63 cached.]
Per-review Opus token consumption (worst case, uncached), both passes:
reviewer: 60,000 input + 8,000 output = 68,000 tokens
critic:   70,000 input + 5,000 output = 75,000 tokens
total:   143,000 tokens per review.
Token-budget ceiling: 40,000 TPM / 143,000 tokens/review ≈ 0.28 reviews/min
→ ≈ 16 reviews/hour (token-limited at 40K TPM).
RPM ceiling: 50 RPM / 2 Opus calls per review = 25 reviews/min
→ RPM is NOT the binding constraint at this call volume.
Prompt-cache effect (issue #148's shared prefix) ON BEDROCK: LiveBedrockModelClient
sends `system` as a flat string with no breakpoint; the ONLY breakpoint is on the
per-review document block. So no system-only (playbook) prefix is ever written,
and nothing caches ACROSS reviews of different documents -- the cross-review
playbook reuse is OpenRouter-only (model-policy/openrouter.json). What Bedrock
does get is the within-review hit: the critic reads the reviewer's cached
system + document prefix (~60K of its 70K input). The reviewer pays in full.
Effective uncached tokens per cached review ≈ (60,000 + 8,000) + (10,000 + 5,000)
Cached throughput ceiling: 40,000 / 83,000 ≈ 0.48 reviews/min
→ ≈ 28 reviews/hour when the within-review cache hits.
[WAS, #148 draft: 53,000 tokens / 45 reviews/hour, which assumed the ~30K
playbook block cached across reviews -- true on OpenRouter only.]
Production volume (2–7/day) is safely under either ceiling.
The eval harness (39 cases × 2 passes × N stochastic runs) is the stress case.
review_throughput_ceiling.bottleneck_model: primary and critic (Opus 4.8, one shared quota)

_derivation: Eval harness worst case (issue #17; roles swapped by issue #136; one model on
both passes since issue #148):
gold_set_cases: 39
passes_per_case: 2  (reviewer + critic)
stochastic_runs: 3  (default; configurable via EVAL_STOCHASTIC_RUNS)
tokens_per_primary_call: ~68,000 (Opus 4.8 reviewer, uncached)
tokens_per_critic_call:  ~75,000 (Opus 4.8 critic, 70K input + 5K output)
Total Opus tokens per full eval run (uncached), both passes:
At 40K TPM this takes ~418 minutes if sequential.
With the shared prefix warm -- on Bedrock that is ONLY the system + document
prefix the reviewer writes and the critic reads within a case; the playbook
does not cache across cases (no system-only breakpoint on Bedrock):
effective tokens/case ≈ 68,000 + 15,000 = 83,000
(A same-case stochastic repeat inside the cache TTL can also hit the reviewer's
system + document prefix; not counted, so this bound is conservative.)
Max parallelism to stay under 40K TPM quota:
Each parallel runner issues one Opus call every ~107s (143K / 2 calls / 40K TPM × 60).
Two parallel runners exceed the quota → ThrottlingException.
Safe parallelism = 1 runner at a time per 40K-TPM account.
Exception: if quota is increased, update max_runners below.
Rate-limiting strategy: both passes run on Opus 4.8, so the eval harness
serializes ALL review calls (one in-flight Opus call at a time) through ONE
token-bucket with a 40K TPM refill rate -- primary_rate_limit_tpm and
critic_rate_limit_tpm below are the same bucket, not two. Running a case's
critic straight after its reviewer also keeps the within-case cache warm.
max_eval_parallelism.rate_limit_strategy: token-bucket — one shared 40K-TPM Opus bucket; serialize reviewer and critic calls

_note: ThrottlingException retries from the pipeline or the eval harness must NOT
fire the 'Bedrock invocation errors > 0' CloudWatch alarm.  They are an
expected operational signal when approaching quota, handled by exponential
backoff retry, and must be tracked as a separate 'ThrottlingException retries'
Alarm split (see ARCHITECTURE.md → Observability and RUNBOOK.md → Incident response):
- 'Bedrock invocation errors > 0'  : fires on non-throttle errors only
These indicate a genuine problem requiring human investigation.
- 'Bedrock throttle retries > N'   : fires when ThrottlingException retry
count exceeds N in a 5-minute window, indicating sustained quota pressure.
Informational by default; escalated if retries cause SLA misses.
Error alarm: filter on Bedrock errorCode NOT IN ('ThrottlingException')
Throttle alarm: filter on Bedrock errorCode = 'ThrottlingException'
